outcome: blood-brain barrier injury (cerebrospinal fluid claudin-5 and MMP-9 concentrations)
neuroinflammation (cerebrospinal fluid Interleukin-8, Interleukin-6, Interleukin-10, stem cell factor levels)
cohort: The study included women with eclampsia, pre-eclampsia (with or without end-organ complications), and normotensive pregnancies who were admitted to Tygerberg Hospital, Cape Town, South Africa, and underwent caesarean delivery.
finding: Women with eclampsia exhibited increased cerebrospinal fluid concentrations of blood-brain barrier injury markers (claudin-5, MMP-9) and pro-inflammatory cytokines (Interleukin-8, Interleukin-6, Interleukin-10), alongside reduced neuroprotective markers (stem cell factor) compared to normotensive controls.
